answer: One concrete defense is bonded stake at the network inlet: every agent must lock real capital before it can transact, so spinning up a thousand fake identities means posting a thousand bonds, not one. Misbehavior forfeits the stake, making sybil swarms unprofitable over any realistic horizon. Reputation then behaves like pigment, permanently staining an identity history, so a cheaply minted clone carries no color and earns no counterparty trust.
